scope: Review leads C/D and adjacent JSONL admission/drain; source working tree before final packaging

initialSandboxRun.notes: Health cache and JSONL lifecycle failures reproduced. Six HTTP cases could not bind task-owned 127.0.0.1 listeners: EPERM. This was not counted as HTTP behavior evidence.

preRepairLoopbackRun.notes: Escalated local run loaded pre-repair modules before source edits. Confirmed stale health cache/readiness; exporter resumed retry, split chunks and gzip continuation after close; JSONL close/flush settled before initialization-delayed admitted writes. Active request case reached its 2-second test bound. Existing late health identity guard, normal exporter retry and runtime cancellation controls passed.

postRepairLoopbackRun.notes: Task-owned loopback server requests only; no outbound exporter, service, dependency installation, sibling edits or publication. All owned listeners, sockets and temporary files cleaned up.

changes.health: Registration invalidates the name cache, and a registration disposer only removes its own record. Existing late-callback cache identity guard remains. Explicit unregister(name) keeps its meaning.
changes.httpExporter: Tracks admissions before user formatting, owns close cancellation, checks terminal state before chunks/requests and after compression, cancels retries and active requests, destroys its agent, drains admitted exports and coalesces repeated close.
changes.jsonl: Tracks complete admitted write operations before initialization; flush includes those operations and close synchronously closes admission before draining all previously admitted writes across kinds.

compatibility.httpClose: Already admitted but interrupted exports reject with MONITOR_EXPORTER_CLOSED. Calls entering after close retain false. Successfully HTTP-acknowledged earlier split chunks remain counted.
compatibility.fileClose: Post-close writes retain {written:0,closed:true}; accepted pre-close writes are drained, not discarded. Flush waits for operations admitted before that flush snapshot.

limits: An HTTP acknowledgement is not a durability guarantee. Closing cannot undo telemetry already received remotely; an aborted active request has uncertain remote delivery and no successful acknowledgement counter.
The formatter remains synchronous trusted code. JavaScript cannot cancel synchronous blocking code, and native gzip must complete its already admitted work before the export promise settles.
JSONL drain waits for filesystem/initialization promises. A host-overridden non-cooperative initializer or stuck filesystem can remain active; runtime cleanup bounds do not forcibly cancel such work.
This receipt describes the source regression run. Final source and exact-tarball consumer runs are recorded separately by the coordinating agent.
